_comment: Production config for serving the SolarEdge inverter to this plant's readers. Three deliberate choices: (1) no poll ranges, so the proxy issues no requests of its own and the inverter only ever sees what the client asks for; (2) a 1 s upstream response timeout: this proxy holds the plant's ONLY device connection, so one hung read stalls every reader - 1 s bounds that. The device answers in ~50-100 ms (p95 measured 161 ms), so 1 s is ~10x headroom; and 1 s keeps the proxy clearly under the default 6 s timeout of the charging app's Modbus client (evcharge/drivers/modbus.py), so the app always receives this proxy's clean exception (0x0B) instead of its own socket timeout. Until 2026-10-03 this was 1 s for a different and now obsolete reason - a SunSpec model scan probing address 50000, which this inverter never answers, where a longer proxy timeout let the client give up first ('i/o timeout', then 'not a SunSpec device'). That client is gone: the logs of 14.09.-03.10. contain no read in the 50000-56999 range at all, while the value had drifted to 5.0 unnoticed. Check after any change here: upstream_timeouts must stay 0 (it was 0 over 6.9 days at 5.0) - if it rises, 1 s is too tight; (3) ondemand_ttl 10 s: with no poll ranges every cached span comes from an on-demand fetch, so this is the window in which two readers asking for the same registers (the charging app's inverter and meter blocks overlap) share one device read instead of issuing two. The cost is that a reader can act on data up to 10 s old - but only up to: past the TTL an expired span is NEVER handed out. If nothing new could be read the client gets the error (exception 0x0B), because on the wire a served leftover is indistinguishable from a fresh reading. Set logging.level to DEBUG and log_every_request to true to trace every request.
